## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
```

for Loops 
- one way to do interative process (what is happening)
- come in handy is in population modeling and Bayesian modeling, for example. They are also integral to programming and happen “under the hood” whether you use them or not.
- two major parts: an indexing statement and a command (or set of commands) to repeat. 
- running this means you run
- starts with for (indexing "in") sequence

for (index in sequence) {
  command to repeat
}

Asking R to print a statement telling us what year it is along a sequence of years.

Start with the simple code for one year:
```{r}
print(paste("The year is", 2000))
```

Put into loop, so that way it makes a sequence.
Make loop for everything. This is the simple code but not saved. so we need to pre-allocate space and tell R where this is going to be saved.

```{r}
years <- c(2015:2021)

for (i in years) { #i is index
  print(paste("The year is", i)) # loop over i
}
```
How to do this:

 1. create a tibble
 2. 
 
```{r}
#pre allocate space: empty columns as long as years the vector #never hardcode bc we need this for flexibility since data always change

year_data <- tibble(year = rep(NA, length (years)),
                    year_name = rep(NA, length(years)))

year_data

```
 
Why pre-allocate?

1. useful for huge datasets (Pre-allocating creates the full-size container once, and the loop just fills in the slots. This is an example with 10000 iterations)

For loop - base R hence the $
```{r}
#seq_along: start with the first then move to the next

for (i in seq_along(years)) {
  year_data$year_name[i] <- paste("The year is", years[i])
  year_data$year[i] <- years[i]
}
#in column year_name (need [i] for this to work) 

year_data


```

testing with conductivity path

```{r}

testdata <- read_csv(here("Week_13", "data", "cond_data", "011521_CT316_1pcal.csv"))
```

glimpse slows computer so only do it once and then add #

```{r}
for (i in seq_along(files)) { # loop over each file (1, 2, 3)


}

#Add in the loop over the raw data:
for (i in seq_along(files)) {

  raw_data <- read_csv(paste0(CondPath, "/", files[i]))
  glimpse(raw_data)

}
```


```{r}
for (i in seq_along(files)) {

  raw_data <- read_csv(paste0(CondPath, "/", files[i]))

  cond_data$filename[i] <- files[i]
  cond_data$mean_temp[i] <- mean(raw_data$Temperature, na.rm = TRUE)
  #no need [i] for the mean portion 
  #can substitute this for std or median and others 
  cond_data$mean_sal[i] <- mean(raw_data$Salinity, na.rm = TRUE)

}

cond_data

#try with median to test
for (i in seq_along(files)) {

  raw_data <- read_csv(paste0(CondPath, "/", files[i]))

  cond_data$filename[i] <- files[i]
  cond_data$median_temp[i] <- median(raw_data$Temperature, na.rm = TRUE)
  #no need [i] for the mean portion 
  #can substitute this for std or median and others 
  cond_data$median_sal[i] <- median(raw_data$Salinity, na.rm = TRUE)

}

cond_data
```

PURRRRRRR

MAP FUNCTIONS

 1. map() makes a list
 2. map_lgl() makes a logical vector
 3. map_int() makes an integer vector
 4. map_dbl() makes a double vector
 5. map_chr() makes a character vector
 6. map() + list_rbind() makes a dataframe

set.seed is 
```{r}
#create vector from 1:10

1:10 #a vector from 1 - 10 (do this 10x)

#create list of 10

set.seed(3817)
1:10 |>
  map(rnorm, n = 15) # 15 random numbers from a normal distribution, in a list
```


Calculate the mean of each list element: option 1
```{r}
set.seed(3817)
1:10 |>
  map(rnorm, n = 15) |>
  map_dbl(mean) #result is now vector of type "double"
```


option 2
means x = 1, 2 so forth 
create your own function 
```{r}
set.seed(3817)
1:10 |>
  map(function(x) rnorm(15, x)) |> # make your own function
  map_dbl(mean)
```

option 3: assuming we already created our own fxn 

```{r}
set.seed(3817)
1:10 |>
  map(~ rnorm(15, .x)) |> # changes the arguments inside the function
  map_dbl(mean)
```

option 1 and 2 = flexible 
option  3 dependent on option 2
function is not saved 
 >>> if you create a fxn prior <<<

Using PURRRR 

```{r}
#reminder find the files

CondPath <- here("Week_13", "data", "cond_data")
files <- dir(path = CondPath, pattern = ".csv")

files

#orrrr full file names 

files <- dir(path = CondPath, pattern = ".csv", full.names = TRUE) # saves the entire path
files
```
take my files dataframe
add set_names if you have multiple files 

```{r}
data <- files |>
  set_names() |>
  map(read_csv) |> #taking all files, reading it
  list_rbind (names_to = "filename") |> #stacked files; list go in a "filename" column names
  group_by(filename) |>
  summarise(mean_temp = mean(Temperature, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_sal = mean(Salinity, na.rm = TRUE))
   

data

```
read_csv(files) expects every file to have the same column names and types. If they differ, or you need to clean each file before combining, use a for loop or map().


Other uses: a plot for every file (purrr)
When you want a function’s side effect (saving a file, printing) rather than a returned value, use walk() instead of map().

```{r}
file_names <- dir(path = CondPath, pattern = ".csv") # just the file names

save_temp_plot <- function(file_name) { #make sure everything is the same 
  site_name <- str_remove(file_name, "\\.csv") # use str_remove

  p <- read_csv(paste0(CondPath, "/", file_name)) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = date, y = Temperature)) +
    geom_line() +
    labs(title = site_name, x = "Date", y = "Temperature (°C)")

  ggsave(here("Week_13", "output", paste0(site_name, "_temp.png")),
         plot = p, width = 6, height = 4)
  #get output and get site_name 
  #_temp.png > site_1_temp.png
  #saves times 
}

walk(file_names, save_temp_plot) #moving along fxn and saving it 
#Run save_temp_plot(file_names[1]) first. Once it works for one file, walk() applies it to all of them.
```

a plot for every file (for loop)
```{r}
file_names <- dir(path = CondPath, pattern = ".csv") # just the file names

for (i in seq_along(file_names)) {

  raw_data <- read_csv(paste0(CondPath, "/", file_names[i]))

  site_name <- str_remove(file_names[i], "\\.csv") # drop ".csv" for the title

  p <- ggplot(raw_data, aes(x = date, y = Temperature)) +
    geom_line() +
    labs(title = site_name, x = "Date", y = "Temperature (°C)")

  ggsave(here("Week_13", "output", paste0(site_name, "_temp_loop.png")),
         plot = p, width = 6, height = 4)
}

#check output folder
dir(here("Week_13", "output"), pattern = "_temp.png")
```
